metadata.summary: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have mapped thousands of congenital heart disease (CHD)-associated variants within non-coding regions of the genome. Non-coding variants can alter regulatory mechanisms, such as transcription factor (TF) binding control of gene expression, potentially contributing human diseases. However, with the increasing number of disease-associated variants, comprehensive functional validation remains a significant challenge. In this work, we developed a novel method called SNP Bind-n-Seq to evaluate >3,000 CHD-risk variants for allelic binding for the cardiac TFs NKX2-5, GATA4, and TBX5 in a high-throughput manner. These binding affinity data sets were coupled with a massively parallel reporter assay (MPRA) to screen CHD-risk variant genotype-dependent regulatory activity. We identified 170 variants that exhibit allelic TF binding and 187 that modulate gene expression. Combining both approaches revealed three high-confidence variants with genotype-dependent TF binding, genotype-dependent transcriptional activity, and eQTL behavior in cardiac cells. Collectively, this study provides the first combined high-throughput biochemical and functional genomic evaluation of thousands of CHD-risk variants.

observations.title: Global Evaluation of Congenital Heart Disease-Associated Non-Coding Variants [SELEX]

observations.text: Genetic perturbations can reshape cell populations by altering the relative abundance of specific cell types and states within the profiled population, including increases, decreases and states that become detectable after perturbation. Pooled single-cell screens, such as Perturb-seq, measure such responses at scale. However, only a small fraction of possible perturbations can be tested experimentally. A central challenge is therefore to predict compositional shifts induced by unseen perturbations. Many perturbation-prediction methods do not directly optimize for this outcome; instead, they predict gene-expression responses and infer cell-type and cell-state composition downstream. Surprisingly, we find that even models that accurately predict perturbation-induced changes in average gene expression perform poorly at forecasting these compositional shifts. To address this gap, we present Pop-Corn, a method that directly predicts how a perturbation reshapes cell-type composition without reconstructing gene expression. In the primary T-cell benchmark, Pop-Corn predicted the overall cell-state composition of held-out perturbations more accurately than the evaluated expression-prediction pipelines, while better preserving the diversity of observed cell states. We further extend Pop-Corn to intact tissue, where it predicts perturbation-induced cell-type proportion changes in local cellular neighborhoods and uses attention patterns to generate hypotheses about context-dependent cellular interactions. Retrospective virtual screens support the use of Pop-Corn to prioritize perturbations for experimental follow-up according to their predicted effects on cell-state composition.
observations.title: Pop-Corn: Predicting Perturbation Phenotype Effects Across Single-Cell and Spatial Contexts

metadata.summary: Uncovering the mechanisms directing the first step of organ formation is essential to understand developmental disorders or regenerative processes. However, the study of early organogenesis in humans remains challenging due to the difficulty to access primary tissues and the lack of in vitromodels which faithfully model this tissue complexity.  Here, we address this limitation in the context of the hepatobiliary system by identifying culture conditions which produce a heterogeneous population of pancreatic, hepatic and biliary progenitors combined with cardiac- and endothelial-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells. When grown in 3D, these different cells self-organised into ‘HepBud’ organoids recapitulating functional structures of the hepatobiliary region of the primitive gut tube. Single-nuclei RNA sequencing confirms that the differentiation of these organoids follows a natural path of development while uncovering novel cellular interactions involved in this process. Critically, we show that the tissues generated by our approach are functional since they contain organ-specific foetal stem cells, such as hepatoblasts, which can differentiate into hepatocytes and cholangiocytes following engraftment into perfused human livers. Utilising our model, we also uncovered novel regulators of early hepatic fate emergence including the transcription factor SOX4 and the EGF signalling pathway. To conclude, the HepBud system demonstrates that early progenitors generated in vitro display the capacity to self-organise into complex organ buds with high developmental potential, hereby providing an accessible model to study mechanisms currently impossible to apprehend in humans.

metadata.summary: Matrin-3 is a DNA- and RNA-binding protein, and its disruption in mice and humans is associated with bicuspid aortic valve, aortic coarctation and patent ductus arteriosus. However, the role of endothelial matrin-3 in atherosclerosis has not been previously studied. Here, bulk RNA-sequencing identified hundreds of differentially expressed in human endothelial cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that the enriched pathways relate to DNA replication, p53 signaling, cell cycle, and cellular senescence. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, endothelial cell-specific matrin-3 deficiency leads to a 35.7% increase in atherosclerotic lesion areas independent of macrophage infiltration, while associated with increased levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides in plasma and total cholesterol and triglycerides in the liver as well as altered transcriptome in the aortic intima. Single-nucleus RNA-seq revealed that endothelial matrin-3 deficiency impairs signaling and promotes inflammation in hepatocytes. Finally, matrin-3 expression was reduced in mouse and human atherosclerotic plaques. These results demonstrate that endothelial matrin-3 limits cellular senescence, which maintains lipid homeostasis via paracrine effects; its expression in the vascular endothelium protects mice from the development of atherosclerosis.

observations.title: Endothelial Matrin-3 Limits Cellular Senescence and Lipid Dysregulation to Protect Against Murine Atherosclerosis [RNA-Seq Aortic intima]

metadata.summary: Cerebral cortical development is a finely regulated process, depending on key neuronal progenitors, giving rise to post-mitotic neurons that migrate to superficial regions in the developing brain. Disruptions can give rise to severe cortical malformations that are associated with intellectual disability and intractable epilepsy. Mutations in EML1/Eml1, coding for a microtubule (MT)-associated protein, lead to subcortical heterotopia (SH) in both humans and mice. In developing mutant mouse brains, ectopic apical radial glia (aRG) progenitors were found outside the normal proliferative ventricular zone (VZ). The normal role of Eml1 in these cells remains to be precisely determined. Using proteomics and imaging approaches, we compared brain tissue from control and mutant mice and identified microtubule and organelle dysregulation. Eml1 influences the trafficking of organelles to different compartments of aRG, where they may be involved in local functions. Thus, we find that mitochondrial and polysome distribution are altered in mutant conditions. Indeed, Eml1 interacts with translational machinery, and an overall downregulation of translation is observed when analysing the translatome of Eml1 mutant aRG. Paradoxically, an upregulation of translation-related mRNAs is also observed. These new data uncover an unprecedented function of Eml1, as well as associating novel subcellular patho-mechanisms with severe heterotopia formation.

metadata.summary: Catecholamine-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is associated typically with mutations in genes encoding Ryanodine Receptor type 2 (RYR2) and Calsequestrin 2 (CASQ2). RyR2 and Casq2 along with membrane proteins, junctin and triadin, constitute the Ca2+ release channel in the junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum in mammalian cardiomyocytes. Mouse models ablating the Casq2 gene phenocopy CPVT have been used to understand the molecular defects underlying the disease and to identify novel therapies. In this study we analyze roles for development and normal aging in the cardiac dysfunctions of Casq2-mutant mice. We show that aging intensifies the disease phenotype. Age-dependent changes in triadin but not in RyR2 or junctin correlate with a more severe CPVT phenotype. We also examine transcriptomes at 1 month and 2 years of age. We identify 583 genes whose expression is dependent on Casq2 genotype with enrichment for genes associated with calcium handling and transport, sarcomere structures, extracellular matrix, and stress signaling associated with cardiac failure. 37% of the differentially expressed genes are specifically dysregulated in older mice. These findings establish aging as a powerful modifier of CPVT and suggest that targeting structural protein dynamics and compensatory transcriptional pathways may offer new therapeutic strategies.

observations.title: Impact of aging on catecholaminergic ventricular arrhythmia and cardiac transcriptome of cardiac calsequestrin null mice

observations.text: Proteins naturally adopt multiple conformations in mediating cellular processes, and ensemble models are used to fit X-ray crystallography data that captures this heterogeneity. In practice, ensemble refinement produces only minor improvements in agreement with experimental data (R-free) over single-conformation models. It has recently been shown that ensemble models are universally trapped, or "tangled"; refinement algorithms strain each individual conformation in the model to fit the electron density in its immediate vicinity, missing more harmonious ways to arrange the collection of protein conformations to fit the electron density. Here, we demonstrate that this type of trap may be escaped by formulating the construction of low-energy conformations from individual conformer coordinates as an integer linear programming problem. The method successfully recovered the two original protein conformations from a previously published synthetic dataset that traps current refinement methods. Inclusion of the method in an automated refinement procedure with real data is shown to improve R-free and reduce geometric strain in a four-conformation model by comparison with controls. Applying this method in combination with human input and fitting low-occupancy waters to density features in the bulk solvent, we produce models for deposited datasets of three separate 14-19 kDa proteins with greatly improved geometry and R-factors. This includes a 0.77 [A] six-conformation model of the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1 (PDB ID: 44PS) with an R-work of 4.7% and an R-free of 6.4%.
observations.title: Optimizing the connectivity of protein conformations to untangle ensemble refinement

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI), a leading cause of global death, results from an irreversible loss of cardiomyocytes. Mammalian hearts possess full regeneration capacity in response to injury in neonates but lose this capacity in adulthood, though the cellular and molecular basis remains unclear. Elucidating this basis is critical for developing regenerative therapies for MI. By integrating three-dimensional cryo-fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography with mosaic analysis with double markers lineage-tracing mice, we elucidate the spatiotemporal dynamics of cardiomyocyte proliferation from birth to adulthood. It reveals a sharp developmental decline in de novo cardiomyocyte formation, characterized by unbiased regional distribution and functional maturation within 72 hours. In adult mice, MI induces a 10-fold expansion of cardiomyocytes re-entering the cell cycle in ischemic regions, yet the cell cycle predominantly arrests before cytokinesis thereby failing to produce new cardiomyocytes. Multi-model transcriptomics identified enoyl-CoA hydratase 1 (ECH1) as a pivotal regulator (repressor) of cardiomyocyte cytokinesis. Genetic ablation of Ech1 in adult mice enhances cardiomyocyte proliferation and improves post-MI cardiac repair. Mechanistically, ECH1 modulates intracellular crotonyl-CoA levels, thereby regulating H3K27 crotonylation and transcription of cytokinesis-associated genes Plk1 and Ect2 in cardiomyocytes. This study uncovers a novel metabolic-epigenetic axis regulating postnatal cardiomyocyte proliferation and positions ECH1 as a promising therapeutic target to overcome cytokinetic blockade to promote cardiomyocyte regeneration, thereby replacing those cardiomyocytes killed after MI.

observations.title: Cryo-fMOST-integrated multi-omics unveils cardiomyocyte proliferation dynamics and novel molecular determinant ECH1 for heart regeneration [Aurkb]

observations.text:
ObjectiveTo compare the accuracy, cost, and speed of a low-cost, non-generative structured-judgment model and four general-purpose large language models (LLMs) for extracting smoking status, pack-years, and quit date from clinical notes to support lung cancer screening (LCS) clinical decision support (CDS).

Materials and MethodsWe built a synthetic, shareable benchmark of 3,000 outpatient notes in three conditions: 1,000 template-generated notes, 1,000 realistic, "messy" notes written by an LLM from structured facts, and 1,000 "messy" notes that required complex arithmetic to determine pack-years and quit dates. Ground truth reference labels were programmatically generated before each note was created. We compared TypeSafe Jev 1.13 with Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Sol, each using an identical structured output schema. We determined United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) 2021 and American Cancer Society (ACS) 2023 eligibility from each systems output in code.

ResultsJev made the correct eligibility decision for 99.1%, 99.9%, and 94.4% of notes in the three conditions, compared with 97.8%, 98.4%, and 98.1% for Haiku, 100.0%, 99.6%, and 99.8% for Sonnet, 99.7%, 98.8%, and 98.5% for Luna, and 100.0%, 99.8%, and 99.6% for Sol. In the complex condition, Jev produced 27 false positive and 14 false negative screening flags per 1,000 notes, the most of any system. Luna cost $0.12 to $0.21 per 1,000 notes and Jev $0.61 to $0.64, compared with $2.44 to $4.22 for Sol, $3.37 to $4.43 for Haiku, and $3.76 to $6.61 for Sonnet. Jev was the fastest system (median 0.45 to 1.21 seconds per note, compared with 1.71 to 3.50 seconds for the others).

DiscussionAll models tested had high accuracy. The structured-judgment model had the lowest latency, which could allow for synchronous use in clinical decision support systems rather than batched, cached invocation. The cost of the structured-judgment model was low, but the newest cost-efficient LLM, Luna, was less expensive and more accurate on the complex notes, though its latency was higher. Accuracy, latency, and cost are all moving quickly as new models are released.

ConclusionFast, low-cost language models could make real-time, note-based CDS practical, and current models are highly accurate. Prices and capabilities are changing rapidly, so continuous benchmarking and system updates are essential.
observations.title: Extracting smoking history from clinical notes for lung cancer screening decision support: comparing a structured-judgment model with general-purpose large language models

observations.text: The development of speech in human children is a protracted process that depends on social experience. From early life, young children produce vocalizations in the presence of others, which affords unique opportunities for feedback about how to communicate successfully. However, for feedback to happen, young childrens speech needs to effect change in the brains of their caregivers. Using dual-brain functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to measure real-time communication between caregivers and their 2- to 3-year-old children (n = 56), we found that children's vocalizations selectively modulated caregivers' brain activity. Parents' brains showed a rapid response to children's production of speech that was communicatively advanced (multiword utterances) vs. less advanced (babble). The findings imply that if part of learning to talk is figuring out how to get your communication partner to listen, then early conversations likely present continuous opportunities for feedback that guide children toward advances in spoken language.
observations.title: Parents' neural dynamics in response to their children's speech

metadata.summary: Aims: Sinoatrial node (SAN) dysfunction is commonly observed in obesity and diabetes and is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Cardiac steatosis, characterized by excessive intracellular lipid droplet (LD) accumulation in cardiomyocytes, is common in these metabolic disorders, but its direct contribution to SAN dysfunction remains unclear. We investigated whether intracellular LD accumulation impairs SAN automaticity. Methods and Results: Transgenic mice (TG) with cardiomyocyte-specific overexpression of perilipin 2 (PLIN2) and double-transgenic mice (DTG) co-expressing PLIN2 and hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) were studied. TG mice exhibited marked LD accumulation in SAN myocytes together with prolonged and highly variable R–R intervals on electrocardiography (ECG). Optical Ca²⁺ mapping of SAN–atrial preparations demonstrated displacement of the leading pacemaker site toward peripheral nodal and extranodal regions in TG mice. Isolated TG SAN myocytes exhibited reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca²⁺ content, attenuated local Ca²⁺ releases (LCRs), and elevated intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. In contrast, mitochondrial and SR ultrastructure were unaltered, and global gene expression profiles were preserved, except for PLIN2 overexpression. Normalization of intracellular LD accumulation by HSL co-expression prevented abnormalities in ECG, SAN automaticity, intracellular Ca²⁺ handling, and ROS levels despite persistent PLIN2 overexpression. This study was limited by the use of male mice, and the causal contribution of elevated ROS to the observed SAN dysfunction was not directly tested. Conclusion: Intracellular LD accumulation alone was sufficient to alter intracellular Ca²⁺ handling and impair SAN automaticity. Normalization of intracellular LD accumulation by HSL co-expression prevented SAN dysfunction, supporting a causal role for intracellular LD accumulation in pacemaker dysfunction. These findings identify myocardial steatosis as a previously underrecognized contributor to SAN dysfunction.

observations.title: Excess accumulation of intracellular lipid droplet impairs sinoatrial function in a mouse model of myocardial steatosis

metadata.summary: Background and Aims: While inflammation and (auto-)immunity are modifiers of atherosclerosis, immunological determinants of cardiovascular risk beyond the established inflammatory markers, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) remain incompletely defined in humans. This exploratory proof-of-concept study aimed to detect immunological signals enriched in patients with increased cardiovascular risk. Methods: A nested case-control study was performed within the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort, a single-center prospective study of 3,316 patients. 44 individuals with and without angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease (CAD) and defined survival status were selected for comprehensive immunophenotyping employing bulk RNA-, single-cell RNA-, single-cell TCR-sequencing, mass cytometry, spatial imaging, and cytokine secretion in blood immune cells. Multi-omics Factor Analysis (MOFA) was applied to identify shared transcriptional programs. Readouts were tested for their association with CAD status and cardiovascular mortality and validated in 2 independent cohorts. Results: The integrated analysis strategy revealed immunological signals not detectable with conventional biomarkers, including a prominent signature of cellular proliferation, linked to activation, memory formation, clonal expansion, interferon signaling, and cytokine secretion in T cells. Cell types and transcriptional programs associated with CAD status and poor long-term survival were identified. These associations were independent of established inflammatory markers, hsCRP and IL-6 that originated from myeloid cells. Key findings were replicated across independent cohorts using 136 scRNA-seq datasets. Cellular proliferation was confirmed by protein validation in atherosclerotic plaques, and signatures were evaluated as stratification tools to predict short-term outcomes in ACS. Conclusions: Multi-omic profiling of blood immune cells revealed novel immune signatures associated with CAD, short- and long-term CVD outcomes that are independent of systemic inflammation and may be used as risk stratification tools in the future.

observations.title: Immunological risk identified by single-cell multi-omics is associated with cellular proliferation and poor outcomes in patients with cardiovascular disease

metadata.summary: The myocardium contains three resident macrophage subsets with distinct gene expression and functions in cardiac injury and disease. However, the underlying epigenetic structure of resident cardiac macrophages and the epigenetic signature of each individual subset is poorly understood. Here, we used single-cell and bulk ATAC sequencing to generate a chromatin accessibility landscape of macrophages from the healthy murine myocardium. Bulk sequencing of each subset revealed 2 chromatin accessibility signatures that corresponded with either resident CCR2+ macrophages, or resident CCR2- macrophages that diverged transcriptionally to give rise to TLF+ (TIMD4+LYVE1+FOLR2+) or MHC-IIhi (TLF-) subsets. Footprint analysis demonstrated subset-specific differences in transcription factor binding – particularly, enrichment of AP-1 in CCR2+ macrophages, and increased MAF binding in TLF+ macrophages. Furthermore, we demonstrate that loss of MAF factor MAFB in myeloid cells disrupts TLF+ macrophage-specific gene expression and skews subset composition toward CCR2+ MFs. Finally, we identify a link between the transcription factor IRF8 and MHC-II, in which loss of IRF8 abolished MHC-II expression exclusively in CCR2- subsets but not CCR2+ macrophages. This granular characterization of the epigenetic and transcriptional substructure of cardiac macrophages

observations.text:
BackgroundMulti-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines are proposed for diagnostic support, but when they help or harm is unknown: evaluations use curated case reports, rarely include budget-matched controls, or isolate perspective independence.

MethodsWe compared a single direct call (Ax1), five specialist personas voiced within one context (P), and the same five roles run as isolated, mutually blinded agents integrated by a moderator (MDT), with five repeat runs per case, on 87 clinicopathological conference (CPC) cases, 406 MedCaseReasoning cases, 364 emergency-department encounters, and a protocol-frozen 392-vignette replication cohort, scored by an LLM judge validated against blinded clinicians, with a three-physician blinded safety rating of the discordant pairs.

FindingsOn curated vignettes the moderated team improved the pre-specified recall endpoints, not top-1 accuracy (CPC +5{middle dot}5, MedCaseReasoning +3{middle dot}0, replication +3{middle dot}3 points at top-3; p = 0{middle dot}0079, 0{middle dot}0079, 0{middle dot}0013); a factorial attributed the gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas. On 364 real emergency notes (labels: clinicians working diagnoses, 46% symptom-level), the direction reversed (top-3 -6{middle dot}4 points, p = 0{middle dot}0022), widened with objective results, and replicated in a second open-weight family. A five-corpus dose-response is consistent with input curation driving the sign (post hoc; corpora differ in provenance and granularity). A symptom-permissive output contract closed the reversals breadth end but not its ordering end, and blinded physicians judged neither strategys errors more dangerous (68% ties; a null powered for large effects only).

InterpretationMulti-agent pipelines are input-conditional: they improve differential-list recall (not top-1 accuracy) on curated inputs and underperform on uncurated emergency text -- a label-level reversal without a clinician-judged safety difference. Strategy selection should key on the input and model family, observable before the model runs, as a routing hypothesis; curated-benchmark gains should not be extrapolated to front-line care.

Funding.None.

Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSMulti-agent LLM diagnostic pipelines report substantial gains, but the active ingredient is unsettled (specialist personas, perspective independence, or extra test-time compute), because few studies include budget-matched single-call controls. Evaluation is concentrated on curated case reports; real front-line inputs, where first-contact notes are thin and reference labels are the treating clinicians working diagnoses, have been essentially untested.

Added value of this studyWe isolated perspective independence as the only manipulated variable and traced the gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis. We showed the effect reverses on 364 real emergency-department notes -- a single corpus whose labels are the treating clinicians working diagnoses -- replicated in a second open-weight family under audited zero-data-retention routing, and confirmed the curated-input gain in a protocol-frozen 392-vignette replication cohort that the evaluated flagship model could not have memorized. A five-corpus dose-response and a length-matched filler arm are consistent with input curation, not length or ceiling, as the driver (the protocol-frozen mediation tests for length, ceiling, and answer leakage were uniformly negative, so this reading is post hoc); a protocol-frozen output-contract arm partitions the reversal by endpoint; and a blinded three-physician rating found no clinician-judged safety difference on the discordant pairs -- a null limited to detecting only large preferences -- so the reversal is a measurement-level finding.

Implications of all the available evidenceMulti-agent diagnostic pipelines are input-conditional: beneficial for differential-list breadth on curated inputs, reversed on real first-contact text without a clinician-judged clinical safety difference at a sample powered only for large effects. Benchmark gains and benchmark reversals alike should not be extrapolated to front-line deployment; pipeline selection should key on the input and model family, which are observable before the model is run.

observations.text: Timely detection of fetal distress during labor is a central pursuit of modern obstetric care. The primary measure used in this regard is fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring (echocardiotocography or CTG), which provides a continuous signal during labor. The vast majority of machine learning applications to CTG assume access to a 30 to 60 minute window just prior to delivery, which makes an untenable assumption that the timing of delivery is known. In this work, we reframe the problem as a time-to-event prediction task. We develop deep time-to-event models to predict the joint probability of imminent delivery and fetal acidosis, a biomarker of fetal hypoxia collected from umbilical cord gas after delivery. We develop a framework for this problem, drawing on deep discrete-time survival methods and marked point processes, adapting each to this particular setting (i.e., continuous physiological signals, fully observed events, partially observed labels). One approach dubbed Marked DeepHit accurately estimates delivery within one hour at multiple elapsed-time landmarks, with test-set AUROC of 0.837 [95% CI 0.692-0.970] and 0.935 [0.858-0.964] at 6 and 12 hours into labor, respectively. We find that these models also achieve competitive performance near delivery time compared to prior models trained specifically on the end of tracing, and outperform other clinical feature-based proposals, both on internal and external validation at a second site. These results give a proof-of-principle to support future prospective deployment of AI-EFM during labor.

metadata.summary: BACKGROUND: Haploinsufficiency of the RNA splicing regulator, RBFOX2, has been linked to congenital heart disease (CHD), including hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain unresolved.  METHODS: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) heterozygous or null for RBFOX2 were created and their cardiomyocyte derivatives (iPSC-CMs) characterized in monolayer culture and engineered heart tissues (EHTs). In addition to cellular phenotyping, molecular profiling by RNA-sequencing and eCLIP-sequencing was performed to detect changes in gene expression, exon usage, and RBFOX2 binding. These datasets were integrated with each other to identify RBFOX2-bound RNAs with altered expression and/or splicing and with publicly available datasets from progressive CM differentiation timepoints. Rescue experiments were performed in iPSC-CMs, EHTs, and zebrafish. RESULTS: We demonstrate that RBFOX2 is essential for cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation by driving transcriptome maturation through gene expression- and alternative splicing-based isoform switching in transcripts primarily encoding sarcomere, cytoskeletal, and focal adhesion components, including the critical Z-disc factor alpha-actinin-2 (ACTN2). We further demonstrate that threshold levels of RBFOX2 facilitate autoregulatory splicing at mutually exclusive exons encoding early and late RBFOX2 isoforms with distinct molecular functions. In heterozygous CMs, this threshold is never reached, resulting in isoform imbalance and production of an aberrant transcript, which further reduces functional RBFOX2 mRNA levels below 50% of WT. Finally, we demonstrate that ACTN2 overexpression rescues heterozygous, but not null, phenotypes, suggesting that ACTN2 activates an RBFOX2-dependent mechanosensitive feedback loop that promotes transcriptome maturation. CONCLUSIONS: Our data demonstrate that reduced RBFOX2 dosage and autoregulation stalls CM differentiation by inhibiting transcriptome maturation, contributing to CHD pathogenesis and potentially increasing heart failure susceptibility.

observations.title: RBFOX2 autoregulation promotes cardiomyocyte transcriptome maturation and differentiation

metadata.summary: Phthalates (ortho-phthalic acid esters) are used in a variety of manufacturing processes, particularly as non-covalent plasticizers in the production of flexible PVC. Phthalates are male reproductive toxicants that disrupt the development of the fetal testis, resulting in malformed seminiferous cords, multinucleated germ cells (MNGs), and decreased testosterone production. The effects of anti-androgenic chemicals, including phthalates and other chemicals that decrease testosterone biosynthesis, are dose-additive, which means that the response to a mixture can be predicted based on the sum of the individual chemicals, rather than the sum of the responses to individual chemicals at the given doses. We previously reported that dipentyl phthalate-induced MNGs were a sensitive, dose-dependent effect. To test whether the induction of MNGs by a mixture of phthalates was dose-additive, we treated timed pregnant Sprague Dawley rats to a mixture of nine phthalates from GD 17-21. The mixture was designed such that the nine phthalates would be equipotent for reduction of testosterone, and we used five doses spanning a two-log dose range. Consistent with prior results, we found that the testosterone-reducing effect of the phthalate mixture was dose-additive and dose-dependent. We also report, for the first time, that the effect of phthalates on morphogenesis of the testis, assessed through histology and immunofluorescence, was dose-additive. The effect of the phthalate mixture that had the lowest effect dose was induction of MNGs, with a BMD10 of 9.402 (6.093, 13.13) mg (∑ all phthalates)/kg/d, which is equivalent to a BMD10 of 3.517 (2.275, 4.919) mg DPEP/kg/d, based on relative potency factors. Quantitative analysis of phthalate metabolites in dam serum showed that the metabolites were present in approximately the same relative concentrations as the parent compounds in the dosing mixture, but with lower levels of monocyclohexyl phthalate and monobenzyl phthalate, suggesting that the diesters with bulky ring side chains may be metabolized more slowly than those with linear or branched aliphatic side chains. Proteomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses showed significant decreases in expression of Leydig cell genes and proteins involved in steroid hormone biosynthesis, as well as enrichment of proteins related to lipid and isoprenoid biosynthesis. Proteomic BMD analysis resulted in a lowest BMDmedian of 2.156 (0.204, 27.830), which was within about 3.74-fold of the lowest apical endpoint BMD.

observations.title: Dose-additive and dose-dependent fetal testis toxicity of a nine-phthalate mixture

metadata.summary: Matrin-3 is a DNA- and RNA-binding protein, and its disruption in mice and humans is associated with bicuspid aortic valve, aortic coarctation and patent ductus arteriosus. However, the role of endothelial matrin-3 in atherosclerosis has not been previously studied. Here, bulk RNA-sequencing identified hundreds of differentially expressed in human endothelial cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that the enriched pathways relate to DNA replication, p53 signaling, cell cycle, and cellular senescence. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, endothelial cell-specific matrin-3 deficiency leads to a 35.7% increase in atherosclerotic lesion areas independent of macrophage infiltration, while associated with increased levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides in plasma and total cholesterol and triglycerides in the liver as well as altered transcriptome in the aortic intima. Single-nucleus RNA-seq revealed that endothelial matrin-3 deficiency impairs signaling and promotes inflammation in hepatocytes. Finally, matrin-3 expression was reduced in mouse and human atherosclerotic plaques. These results demonstrate that endothelial matrin-3 limits cellular senescence, which maintains lipid homeostasis via paracrine effects; its expression in the vascular endothelium protects mice from the development of atherosclerosis.

observations.text: Brain synapses are hotspots of energy consumption, and the synaptic plasticity underlying learning sharply increases this demand. Because most synapses lie far from their cell body, their energy demands must be met locally. A dendritic mitochondrion can extend ~30 m and span many spines, yet ramps up ATP synthesis only near spines undergoing plasticity, providing immediate and sustained energy. Whether structural changes in these juxtaspinal mitochondrial regions (2 m segments at spine bases) support this response is unknown; resolving their energy-producing architecture poses substantial challenges. Compared with the lamellar cristae of axonal mitochondria, dendritic mitochondrial cristae form complex, tubular, and interconnected networks that require multiple high-resolution tomograms to characterize. We therefore developed a correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM) pipeline with a custom deep-learning model that simultaneously segments five distinct 3D suborganellar structures from limited training data, enabling quantitative analysis across 42 tomograms at 2 nm pixel resolution. We find that juxtaspinal mitochondrial regions are larger than non-juxtaspinal regions within the same mitochondrion and enlarge further during synaptic plasticity. Juxtaspinal mitochondrial ATP synthesis and spine ATP levels rise in parallel; during single-spine plasticity, ATP rises within minutes, before detectable enlargement, indicating that juxtaspinal mitochondrial enlargement sustains rather than initiates the local energy response. The enlarged regions exhibit increased cristae membrane surface area, crista junction number, and membrane area with high curvature, together with increased MIC60 and ATP synthase copies, endoplasmic reticulum contacts, and more proximal ribosomes. Matrix-targeted PKA inhibition reduces MIC60 phosphorylation and impairs juxtaspinal mitochondrial enlargement, plasticity-associated ATP increase, and single-spine plasticity. Together, our findings support a model in which spine-specific remodeling within an individual mitochondrion boosts local metabolic capacity to sustain ATP synthesis and fuel synaptic plasticity.
observations.title: Mitochondria remodel near synapses to boost metabolic capacity and fuel plasticity

metadata.summary: Alcohol misuse damages numerous organs, including the liver, heart, brain, and pancreas. The kidney remains a severely understudied target of alcohol-induced injury despite renal injury being commonly observed in endstage alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) patients. A 6-week murine ethanol (1-6% v/v) model for earlystage ALD combined with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) treatment was utilized to reveal mechanisms of renal injury. This paradigm yields elevated kidney damage markers when compared to ethanol consumption alone, including elevated urinary KIM-1 in 3 weeks. Hypothesis-generating tissue spatial analysis was used to explore ethanol-related transcriptomic alterations across kidney morphology. Using a publicly available scRNA-seq dataset, the predominant cell-type specific differences were identified and allowed for the generation of spatially resolved gene clusters. Ethanol + CCl4 increased kidney injury marker gene expression in proximal tubule cells, signifying extensive damage. Overall, a decrease in expression of ethanol metabolizing genes was localized to the renal cortex. Genes associated with the unfolded protein response (UPR) were induced across the kidney and were morphologically associated throughout the nephron. Key mRNAs (Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Ndrg1) and ribosomal transcripts were altered due to ethanol metabolism across proximal tubules. Furthermore, epigenetic alterations in regulatory marks of lysine acetylation or trimethylation are associated with the combination treatment. Collectively, the application of tissue spatial transcriptomics to a well-defined model of alcohol toxicity reveals dynamic morphologic changes in gene expression across renal cell types due to ethanol. Our results indicate ER stress and the UPR are significantly impacted by ethanol metabolism throughout proximal tubules, associating with ethanol-induced renal dysfunction.

observations.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals ER stress due to alcohol-induced kidney injury

observations.text: Remarkable progress has been made in the field of protein structure prediction. Representative methods like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold achieve prediction accuracy close to experimental structural determination, but at the cost of heavy computational consumption for model training. In this work, we propose a new framework, Cerebra, for improving the computational efficiency of protein structure prediction. In this network architecture, multiple sets of atomic coordinates are predicted parallelly and their mutual complementarity is leveraged to rapidly improve the quality of predicted structures through a new attention mechanism named Path Synthesis Attention (PSA). Consequently, Cerebra markedly reduces the computational consumption, achieving evident acceleration on both model training and inference, in comparison to OpenFold, the academic version of AlphaFold2. When evaluated on the CAMEO 2025 dataset, the Cerebra model trained on a limited number of GPUs shows a comparable performance to the published OpenFold model that has been thoroughly optimized using a plethora of computational resources. Moreover, ablation studies confirm that the PSA mechanism efficiently accelerates the network convergence, suggesting its potential in handling the many-body effects of protein geometries in graph-based models. Finally, the fast inference of Cerebra effectively assists hallucination-based de novo protein backbone design, allowing the production of abundant backbone structures with sufficient designability and novelty.
observations.title: Cerebra: a computationally efficient framework for accurate protein structure prediction

observations.text: The Vanishing White Matter (VWM) Registry is a single-center database containing longitudinal survey data from >470 untreated patients with DNA- and MRI-confirmed VWM. VWM is a rare genetic disorder of the brains white matter with an estimated live birth incidence of 1 per 100,000 and prevalence of 1.3 per 1,000,000 people in the Netherlands. The Registry represents a remarkably extensive collection of systematically gathered information on this disease, enabling crucial research into the natural history of VWM and providing a valuable resource for control arms in clinical trials. Data, initially collected on paper from 2004, have been maintained electronically since 2018, and include validated scales alongside a disease-specific customized questionnaire covering clinical, functional, and psychosocial domains. Survey packages, available in eight languages, are sent one to four times a year, depending on patient age. Built-in validity checks and review by pediatric and adult neurologists ensure data quality. The dataset is continuously updated with questionnaires expanding its scope, and structured for analysis and reuse in research on VWM.
observations.title: The Vanishing White Matter registry: a unique source of natural history data

observations.text: Accurate prenatal screening from ultrasound imaging is severely constrained by the extreme spatial heterogeneity of fetal structures and the data scarcity inherent to rare congenital anomalies. To overcome these computational bottlenecks, we present RadarMAE, a data-efficient self-supervised representation learning framework tailored for fetal ultrasound analysis. By employing a novel, structure-aware masking strategy, RadarMAE enables robust pre-training on highly limited clinical datasets. Benchmarking the framework on first-trimester screening for trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), our model achieved exceptional diagnostic performance on an internal cohort, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.99, 97% accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 98% specificity. Crucially, through domain-adversarial adaptation, the framework demonstrates robust cross-institutional generalization under extreme source-target data imbalance, bounding performance degradation to[≤] 0.04 across all key metrics in external testing. Furthermore, by integrating spatial registration with explainable AI, we constructed the first population-level facial risk atlas for trisomy 21. This data-driven interpretability framework validates standard clinical markers while revealing the comparable diagnostic weight of underutilized features, such as mandibular dysmorphology. Ultimately, this approach provides a scalable, transparent, and high-performance solution for equitable prenatal diagnostics and phenotypic biomarker discovery.
observations.title: A Structure-Aware Self-Supervised Framework for Transferable Fetal Ultrasound Screening
